title: Security Models and Microsoft Defender for Cloud

header.html: Describe the concept of Zero Trust; Describe the purpose of the defense-in-depth model; Describe the purpose of Microsoft Defender for Cloud
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1Zero Trust

Zero Trust is a security model that does not trust anything by default, even inside the corporate network. Every request is treated as if it came from an open network.

The three guiding principles:

Principle Meaning
Verify explicitly Always authenticate and authorize using all available data: identity, location, device health, service, data classification, anomalies
Use least-privilege access Give only the access needed, limited in time and scope (just-in-time, just-enough access)
Assume breach Design as if an attacker is already inside: segment access, encrypt data, monitor and detect threats

The old model was "trust everything inside the network perimeter". Zero Trust replaces it because users, devices and data are now everywhere (cloud, home, mobile).

Exam tip

. The slogan is "never trust, always verify." A question about MFA, device checks, least privilege and segmentation together describes Zero Trust.

2Defense in depth

Defense in depth uses multiple layers of protection, so if one layer fails the next still protects the data. It aims to slow an attacker and limit damage.

Layer (outer to inner) Protects Azure examples
Physical security Datacenter buildings and hardware Microsoft datacenter controls
Identity and access Who can sign in and what they can do Microsoft Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access, RBAC
Perimeter The edge of the network from large attacks DDoS protection, Azure Firewall
Network Traffic between resources Network security groups, segmentation, private endpoints
Compute Virtual machines and hosts Patching, endpoint protection, restricted access to VMs
Application App code and APIs Secure development, secrets in a vault, app firewalls
Data Stored information (the thing to protect) Encryption, access control, backup

The data is at the center and the layers wrap around it.

Exam tip

. The layers go physical → identity and access → perimeter → network → compute → application → data. The question may ask which layer a service belongs to: Entra ID = identity and access, DDoS protection and firewall = perimeter, NSG = network, encryption = data.

3Microsoft Defender for Cloud

Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a cloud-native application protection platform that does two jobs: it assesses your security posture and it protects workloads from threats. It works for Azure, on-premises (hybrid) and other clouds (multicloud).

Capability What it does
Cloud security posture management (CSPM) Continuously assesses your resources against security best practices, gives a Secure Score and recommendations to fix weaknesses
Cloud workload protection (CWP) Detects and responds to threats against your workloads with Defender plans for servers, storage, databases, containers and more
Regulatory compliance view Shows how your resources measure against compliance standards
Multicloud and hybrid The same view for Azure, on-premises machines (with Azure Arc) and other clouds
  • Secure Score: a percentage that shows how well your resources follow security recommendations; higher is better. Fixing recommendations raises it.
  • Recommendations list what to fix and how, ranked by impact.
  • The foundational posture features are free; advanced protection plans are paid. [Verify live]
Exam tip

. Posture and recommendations and score → Defender for Cloud. Threat protection for VMs, storage, SQL → Defender for Cloud's Defender plans. Hybrid and multicloud protection → Defender for Cloud (with Azure Arc).

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors verifies every request using identity, device health and location, gives users only needed access and assumes attackers may already be inside. Which model is this?

  • APerimeter security
  • BPublic cloud
  • CZero Trust
  • DCapital expenditure
Show the answer

Answer: C. Verify explicitly, least privilege and assume breach are the Zero Trust principles.

S2Which layer of defense in depth does Microsoft Entra ID with MFA protect?

  • APhysical security
  • BData
  • CIdentity and access
  • DPerimeter
Show the answer

Answer: C. Sign-in control and access are the identity and access layer.

S3What is the main idea of defense in depth?

  • AMultiple layers of protection so a failure in one does not expose everything
  • BOne very strong layer is enough to stop every attack
  • CTrust all traffic that starts inside the network
  • DDisable monitoring to save cost
Show the answer

Answer: A. Layers slow attackers and limit damage when a layer fails.

S4Which tool shows a Secure Score and recommendations for improving the security of Azure, on-premises and other cloud resources?

  • AAzure Advisor
  • BMicrosoft Defender for Cloud
  • CAzure Cost Management
  • DAzure Service Health
Show the answer

Answer: B. Defender for Cloud assesses posture, scores it and recommends fixes across hybrid and multicloud.

S5Which Zero Trust principle says to limit users to the minimum access they need?

  • AVerify explicitly
  • BUse least-privilege access
  • CAssume breach
  • DTrust the network
Show the answer

Answer: B. Least privilege restricts access in scope and time.

S6Which layer includes protecting the network edge from a distributed denial-of-service attack?

  • AData
  • BApplication
  • CPerimeter
  • DPhysical
Show the answer

Answer: C. DDoS protection and firewalls defend the perimeter.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What is the slogan of Zero Trust?

Show the answer

Never trust, always verify.

R2Name the three Zero Trust principles.

Show the answer

Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach.

R3Name the seven layers of defense in depth in order.

Show the answer

Physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application, data.

R4What does Defender for Cloud's Secure Score show?

Show the answer

How well your resources follow security recommendations; higher is better.

R5Which two jobs does Defender for Cloud do?

Show the answer

Posture management (assess and recommend) and workload protection (detect threats).

R6Can Defender for Cloud cover non-Azure resources?

Show the answer

Yes, on-premises (hybrid) and other clouds (multicloud).

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Zero Trust never trust, always verify; verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach
Defense in depth layers: physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application, data
Layer examples Entra ID/MFA = identity; DDoS and firewall = perimeter; NSG = network; encryption = data
Defender for Cloud posture (Secure Score, recommendations) plus threat protection; Azure, on-premises and other clouds
